title: NASA targets mid-2027 for SunRISE mission launch
excerpt: The SunRISE mission will use six small satellites to track radio bursts from the Sun's atmosphere.
bodyHtml:
NASA announced on October 6, 2026, that the Sun Radio Interferometer Space Experiment, or SunRISE, mission will launch no earlier than mid-2027.

The mission will utilize a SpaceX Falcon Heavy rocket departing from Kennedy Space Center in Florida as a rideshare with a payload sponsored by the United States Space Force’s Space Systems Command.

The mission consists of six toaster-oven-size small satellites that will operate as one giant radio dish slightly above geosynchronous orbit, which is about 22,000 miles (35,000 kilometers) in altitude. These satellites will track the rumbles of radio bursts coming from within the Sun’s atmosphere, or corona. The bursts are generated by accelerated particles leaving the Sun.

The SmallSats have completed assembly and testing at Utah State University’s Space Dynamics Laboratory in Logan, where they will be stored until they are shipped to Florida shortly before launch. The mission’s science investigation is led by the University of Michigan in Ann Arbor, and the project is managed by JPL, a division of Caltech in Pasadena, California.
